reasons: Only the fixed targets /work/src and /work/build are mounted. The worktree and build dir reach the root shell as positional parameters after realpath -e, so they cannot inject commands. The mounts live in a private namespace (unshare --mount --propagation private); nothing reached the host namespace in the experiments. The command runs as the caller: uid 1000, all capabilities zeroed. sudo removes BASH_ENV and LD_*. The harness user already has NOPASSWD sudo, so this adds no privilege.

Compile commands in a fixed-mode dir (build/int-20f) contain only /work/src and /work/build paths. compile_commands.json, CMakeCache.txt and rules.ninja have no real path, so identical sources give identical ccache keys. The only real path left in build.ninja is the VCS dependency on .git/worktrees/<name>/logs/HEAD. That is a ninja input, not part of any compile command. VCSRevision.h holds the commit hash, which is identical for the same commit and only affects the few TUs that include it.

Legacy dirs are unaffected. pathmode.sh returns legacy for build/int-20, whose CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY is the real path; WT_RUN is then empty and the original arguments are passed as before. The empty-array expansion is fine under set -u on bash 5.2.

lit.sh, integrate.py and cluster_errors.py still work in fixed mode, and concurrent builds are isolated. $out is made absolute and points outside /work, so it is still writable inside the namespace. lit JSON test names are suite-relative, so they match the baseline. lit_diff --worktree is run outside the namespace with the real path. cluster_errors' fallback turns /work/src/{llvm,clang,lld}/... into repo-relative paths, and cluster keys have paths replaced by <path>, so integrate.py's before/after key comparison works across modes. Two concurrent inwt.sh runs on different worktrees each saw only their own /work/src and /work/build. Nested inwt.sh also works.
Failure modes are loud and do no damage. python3 -m unittest discover -s tests: 25 tests OK.

checks.security_experiment: scripts/inwt.sh wt/19-E001 <scratch> id -> uid=1000(ubuntu), the caller's groups. findmnt inside showed /work/src bound to wt/19-E001 and /work/build bound to the scratch dir. Host findmnt /work/src and /work/build afterwards: nothing (findmnt | grep -c /work = 0). /proc/self/status inside: CapPrm/CapEff/CapAmb = 0. mount inside -> 'must be superuser'. A build-dir argument containing ';id' was treated as a literal path. A nonexistent worktree failed in realpath with rc 1. /work, /work/src and /work/build are root-owned 0755, so the user cannot swap a mount target for a symlink.
checks.env_inside_namespace: The caller's env is kept, including CCACHE_* and custom variables. sudo still changes some of it: PATH becomes secure_path (~/.local/bin, holding only claude/codex, drops out), USER and LOGNAME become root, SUDO_* are added, and LD_*, PYTHONPATH and BASH_ENV are removed. All build tools (clang, cmake, ninja, ccache, python3) are in /usr/bin, so builds are unaffected. Non-blocking: a tool that reads USER, or relies on PYTHONPATH or LD_LIBRARY_PATH, would behave differently.
checks.fixed_mode_paths: build/int-20f: CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY=/work/src/llvm. Real paths: 0 in compile_commands.json, 0 in CMakeCache.txt, 0 in rules.ninja; 3 lines in build.ninja, all the VCS dependency on .git/worktrees/int-20/logs/HEAD. The sample compile command (RISCVISelLowering.cpp) uses directory /work/build and -I/work/{src,build} only. lit.site.cfg.py points at /work/src. The build is Release with no -g, so there are no debug-info paths.
checks.legacy_mode: build/int-20 has the real CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY -> legacy mode, same arguments as before. The only difference in lit.sh is that $out is made absolute, which points to the same location.
checks.lit_and_integrate: wlit.sh wt/int-20 build/int-20f -v <test> ran lit inside the namespace. It stopped at 'FileCheck not found in /work/build/bin' only because int-20f is still mid-build. integrate.py runs --build-cmd and --lit-cmd through the shell from the harness root, so they need no change. cluster_errors.relpath('/work/src/clang/lib/Sema/X.cpp') returned 'clang/lib/Sema/X.cpp'.
checks.concurrency: Two inwt.sh runs in parallel (wt/19-E001 with b1, wt/19-E002 with b2) each saw their own gitdir and build-dir contents on every iteration. ccache is safe for concurrent use.

failure_modes.work_dirs_missing: inwt.sh prints 'inwt: /work/src and /work/build must exist (sudo mkdir -p)' and exits 2 before calling sudo.
failure_modes.sudo_unavailable: sudo -n fails with 'a password is required' and rc 1. In build.sh, integrate.py then rejects with 'build failed without recognized error signatures'. In lit.sh the rc is reported as 'RISCVISAInfo unit tests failed or did not run', which is misleading, and lit_diff fails on the missing lit.json. It fails closed, not green.
failure_modes.direct_llvm_lit: Running build/int-20f/bin/llvm-lit outside the namespace fails at once (ModuleNotFoundError: lit, because the script imports from /work/src/llvm/utils/lit), so there is no false pass. A direct ninja -C <fixed dir> should likewise fail on missing /work/src inputs (not tried), and the host /work/build is root-owned, so nothing gets written there. Built tools in <build>/bin run directly (resource dir is relative).
failure_modes.cmake_install: cmake --install of a fixed-mode dir must also go through inwt.sh. It only appears in phase0 for int-18, which is a legacy dir.

non_blocking_notes: A fixed-mode build dir no longer records which real worktree it belongs to: CMake's source-dir mismatch check sees /work/src every time. Running build.sh wt/A build/X and then build.sh wt/B build/X would silently build B incrementally on A's objects. Mtime-based ninja could leave stale objects, and the VCS dependency still points to A. The build-dir-per-worktree naming convention prevents this in practice. A cheap guard would be for inwt.sh or pathmode to write <bd>/.inwt-worktree and refuse a mismatch.
For build-dir files, cluster sites (not keys) now read /work/build/... instead of the per-dir real path, which is actually more consistent across dirs. Keys are unaffected.

wlit.sh maps any non-option argument that exists under the worktree, including the value of an option like --filter X if X happens to be a worktree path. Absolute real test paths are not mapped and fail loudly. Both are cosmetic.
Legacy build/int-20 and fixed worker dirs do not share ccache entries. The fixed-mode integration dir int-20f is what makes workers hit.
When invoked from a terminal, sudo's use_pty gives the command a tty, which only changes how ninja's progress looks. Detached runs via wt.sh have no tty (verified: stdout is not a tty).
checks.sop: The worker.sop.md step 4 change is clear. It tells workers to use scripts/wlit.sh with worktree-relative test paths, explains why (fixed paths for ccache, H005), and says that direct lit only works through wlit.sh or inwt.sh while tools in <build_dir>/bin run directly.
